content: A small number of individuals who have used pimecrolimus cream or similar medications have developed skin cancer or lymphoma, a type of cancer affecting the immune system. However, there is insufficient evidence to confirm whether pimecrolimus cream directly caused these cancers. Research involving transplant patients, laboratory animals, and the mechanism of action of pimecrolimus suggests a potential increased risk of cancer for users of this medication. Further studies are required to better understand this risk. To minimize the potential risk of developing cancer while using pimecrolimus cream, follow these guidelines: Use pimecrolimus cream only when you have active eczema symptoms. Discontinue its use once your symptoms resolve or if your doctor advises you to stop. Avoid prolonged, continuous use of the cream. If your eczema symptoms do not improve after six weeks of using pimecrolimus cream, contact your doctor. You may require an alternative treatment. If your eczema symptoms return after completing treatment with pimecrolimus cream, consult your doctor. Apply the cream only to areas of skin affected by eczema. Use the smallest amount necessary to control your symptoms. Do not use pimecrolimus cream to treat eczema in children under the age of 2 years. Inform your doctor if you have a history of cancer, particularly skin cancer, or any condition that affects your immune system. Protect your skin from both natural and artificial sunlight while using pimecrolimus cream. Avoid sunlamps, tanning beds, and ultraviolet light therapy. Your doctor or pharmacist will provide you with a Medication Guide from the manufacturer when you begin treatment with pimecrolimus and each time you refill your prescription. Read this information carefully and ask your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. You can also access the Medication Guide on the FDA website or the manufacturer’s website. Discuss the risks of using pimecrolimus with your doctor. Pimecrolimus is prescribed to manage the symptoms of eczema (atopic dermatitis), a skin condition characterized by dryness, itching, and sometimes red, scaly rashes. This medication is intended for patients who cannot use other eczema treatments or whose symptoms are not adequately controlled by other medications. Pimecrolimus belongs to a class of drugs known as topical calcineurin inhibitors, which work by suppressing the immune system's production of substances that contribute to eczema. Pimecrolimus cream is applied to the skin, typically twice daily, for up to six weeks at a time. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and consult your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Use the cream exactly as directed, without applying more or less than prescribed. Pimecrolimus cream is for external use only. Avoid contact with your eyes or mouth. If the cream gets into your eyes, rinse them with cold water. If swallowed, contact your doctor immediately. To apply the cream: 1. Wash your hands with soap and water. 2. 3. Apply a thin layer of pimecrolimus cream to all affected areas, including the head, face, and neck if necessary. 4. Gently and thoroughly rub the cream into the skin. 5. Wash your hands again with soap and water to remove any residual cream, unless your hands are being treated. 6. You may wear normal clothing over treated areas but avoid using bandages, dressings, or wraps. 7. Do not wash off the cream from treated areas. Avoid swimming, showering, or bathing immediately after application. Consult your doctor about reapplying the cream if it is washed off. 8. Once the cream is fully absorbed, you may apply moisturizers, sunscreen, or makeup to the treated areas. Discuss the use of specific products with your doctor. Before using pimecrolimus cream: Inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to pimecrolimus or any other medications. Provide a complete list of all prescription and nonprescription medications, vitamins, supplements, and herbal products you are taking. Certain medications, such as antifungals, calcium channel blockers, and others, may interact with pimecrolimus. Notify your doctor if you have or have ever had Netherton’s syndrome, widespread skin redness and peeling, other skin diseases, or skin infections such as chickenpox, shingles, herpes, or eczema herpeticum. Also, inform your doctor if your eczema rash is crusty, blistered, or appears infected. Inform your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. If you become pregnant while using pimecrolimus, contact your doctor. Discuss the safe use of alcohol during treatment, as consuming alcohol may cause facial flushing or redness. If exposed, contact your doctor immediately. Good skin care and moisturizers can help alleviate eczema-related dryness. Consult your doctor about appropriate moisturizers and apply them after using pimecrolimus cream. Discuss with your doctor whether you should avoid consuming grapefruit or grapefruit juice while using this medication. If you miss a dose, apply it as soon as you remember. If it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue your regular schedule. Do not apply extra cream to compensate for a missed dose. Mild side effects of pimecrolimus may include: Burning, warmth, stinging, soreness, or redness at the application site (contact your doctor if this persists for more than one week). Warts, bumps, or other skin growths. Eye irritation. Headache. Cough. Nasal symptoms such as redness, congestion, or runny nose. Nosebleeds. Diarrhea. Painful menstrual periods. Severe side effects require immediate medical attention and include: Sore or red throat. Fever or flu-like symptoms. Ear pain, discharge, or signs of infection. Hives. New or worsening rash. Itching. Swelling of the face, throat, tongue, lips, eyes, hands, feet, ankles, or lower legs. Difficulty breathing or swallowing. Crusting, oozing, blistering, or other signs of skin infection. Cold sores, chickenpox, or other blisters. Swollen glands in the neck. Report any unusual or severe side effects to your doctor. Serious side effects can also be reported to the FDA’s MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program. Store pimecrolimus cream in its original container, tightly sealed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Dispose of expired or unused medication properly, and consult your pharmacist for disposal instructions. Keep all medical appointments while using this medication. Do not share it with others. Consult your pharmacist if you have questions about refilling your prescription. Brand name: Elidel®
